messages.subject: what's wrong with the colors
parts:
Hi guys,
Happy new year!
who can tell me what is wrong with the code. I want to highlight the box with different color. but the colors for boxes are totally wrong, you can see: blue for red box, grey90 for green box, red for blue box. legend also not corect. I use these code:
mpg %>% mutate(type=ifelse(class=="subcompact","red",

                            ifelse(class=="midsize","blue",

                                   "grey90" ))) %>% 

  ggplot(aes(x=class,y=hwy,fill=type))+geom_boxplot().

messages.author: 942ffec526d6a312
messages.subject: Re: what's wrong with the colors
parts:
Hi,

> Happy new year!

And a very happy new year to you.

> who can tell me what is wrong with the code. I want to highlight the box
> with different color. but the colors for boxes are totally wrong, you
> can see: blue for red box, grey90 for green box, red for blue box.
> legend also not corect. I use these code:
> mpg %>% mutate(type=ifelse(class=="subcompact","red",
>
>                             ifelse(class=="midsize","blue",
>
>                                    "grey90" ))) %>%
>
>   ggplot(aes(x=class,y=hwy,fill=type))+geom_boxplot().

Your type variable is being converted on the fly to a factor,
and by default this isbeing done alphabetically - blue is first,
gey90 second and red third. You are colouring by this factor,
but applying the default colour scheme, so getting blue as reddish
etc.

I'd do it something more like this (note: untested code typed into
this email):

mpg %>% mutate(type=ifelse(class %in% c("subcompact", "midsize"),
class, "other"),
type=factor(type, levels = c("subcompact", "midsize",
"other"))) %>%
ggplot(., aes(x=class, y=hwy, fill=type)) + geom_boxplot() +
scale_fill_manual(values = c('red', 'blue', 'grey90')) + theme_bw()

I added the theme_bw as your grey90 boxes will clash with the
grey background.

Hope this helps.

Ron.
